description: MCP server for Infino — keyword (BM25), semantic, hybrid, and SQL retrieval plus writes over your data on object storage or Infino Cloud, from Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, or any MCP client.
rules: The server is launched by the MCP client over stdio as 'npx -y @infino-ai/mcp-server'; never run it by hand in normal use. All configuration is environment variables — there are no config files and no command-line flags.

Claude Code: 'claude mcp add infino --scope user -e INFINO_MCP_URI=<path-or-uri> -- npx -y @infino-ai/mcp-server'. One-step plugin install: '/plugin marketplace add infino-ai/infino-mcp' then '/plugin install infino@infino-ai'.

INFINO_MCP_URI names the data to serve: a local path, an s3:// or az:// bucket URI, or a hosted https://<host>/<database> Infino Cloud endpoint. Unset, it defaults to the durable per-user directory ~/.infino/mcp.

A hosted https:// URI requires INFINO_API_KEY (an inf_ key from the Infino Cloud console); the database is the URI's last path segment. If the database answers 404, call infino_create_database once — it is idempotent and a no-op locally.

Storage credentials come from the environment: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY for S3 (set AWS_ENDPOINT_URL for R2, MinIO, or B2), AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT / AZURE_STORAGE_KEY for Azure Blob. They are never logged or returned.

Embedding is local by default (transformers.js all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384 dims, no key; a one-time ~90 MB download). Set INFINO_MCP_EMBED_PROVIDER=openai plus INFINO_MCP_EMBED_BASE_URL and INFINO_MCP_EMBED_API_KEY for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
Queries are embedded in this server even against a hosted table, so INFINO_MCP_EMBED_MODEL must match the model that produced the table's stored vectors; a dimension mismatch fails at search time.

Search tools: infino_semantic_search (meaning; score is a distance, lower is closer), infino_keyword_search (BM25; higher is better, mode 'or' or 'and'), infino_hybrid_search (BM25 + vector fused by reciprocal-rank fusion). Responses carry score_kind.

Unranked filters: infino_token_match (rows containing the tokens), infino_exact_match (equality on an indexed column), infino_count (tally of keyword matches without fetching rows). infino_list_tables and infino_describe_table inspect the catalog.

infino_sql runs one statement (DDL/DML included). The engine's search functions are SQL table functions, so one query can rank and aggregate; pass a vector via a {{name}} placeholder filled from the embed map, e.g. embed {"q": "query text"}.

The 'columns' argument on every search tool is a projection passed to the engine: any table column can come back per hit. It defaults to the text column, with _id and score always included; nothing is truncated — project fewer columns or lower k.

Writes are always available; there is no write gate and the retired INFINO_MCP_ENABLE_WRITES variable is ignored. On Infino Cloud a read-scoped API key is refused every write. Locally, point the server only at data the agent may change.

infino_create_table takes a {column: type} descriptor; 'fts' picks full-text columns (default: every large_utf8) and 'vector: true' adds an embedding column sized to the server's embedder with a cosine index — the agent never types a dimension.

infino_add_documents appends rows, one call = one commit; rows without a vector are embedded from the text column in one batch. infino_update_documents and infino_delete_documents take a SQL predicate and work on durable storage only.
A tool call carries tens of documents. For a whole corpus, ingest with the infino CLI ('infino ingest' takes Parquet or NDJSON against the same URI) or an SDK, then search it through the server.
Every tool carries MCP annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint) so the client can confirm destructive calls. Logs go to stderr, never stdout, so they cannot corrupt the JSON-RPC stream.
